text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Opposition Greens claim they have documents to prove that Austrian prosecutors refused to issue an arrest warrant for one of the alleged killers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989.

- Chancellor Viktor Klima says European integration will not mean the end for Austria's independent foreign policy and insists Austria has to await the future development of NATO before it decides on a possible membership.
- The far-right Freedom Party plans to launch its own labour union on May 1.
- The government plans to introduce a road pricing system for trucks on Austrian motorways by the year 2000.

- The government and the civil servants' union have agreed on looking into ways of saving money in the public sector. Consulting firm Arthur D. Little claims in a study up to 70,000 public sector jobs could be cut.
- Flag carrier Austrian Airlines aims to almost triple pre-tax profits to about 300 million schillings in the current year.
- Italy's telecommunications company Stet to become the new strategic partner of state-owned mobile phone company Mobilkom.
- Brick maker Wienerberger to pay an unchanged dividend of 42 schillings per share despite of a 4.3 percent fall in 1996 operating profit.
- Linz Textil 1996 net profit down 50 million schillings at 104.2 million, but the company says it expects earnings to rise in the current year.
- Water treatment company BWT 1996 pre-tax profit rises to record 231.1 million schillings in 1996, from 191.4 million a year earlier.
- German truck maker MAN to list its shares on the Vienna stock exchange.
DIE PRESSE
- President Thomas Klestil is likely to be re-elected should he stand for a second term next year, even though former chancellor Franz Vranitzky's popularity has soared.
- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, secretary of state in the finance ministry, says the government should work closely together with labour unions in preparation for Europe's single currency.

- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel said the government should not replace its chief euro promoter Gustav Raab, who resigned last week amid charges he towed the European Commission's official line on the single currency.
- Engineering group VA Technologie plans to invest some eight billion schillings in new acquisitions in Europe, aimed at boosting group turnover by a third by the year 2000.
- A planned reduction of Austria's trade deficit by 10.5 billion schillings this year will be impossible without the government's help, analysts say.
KURIER
- Social Affairs Minister Lore Hostasch plans cuts in pensions to help save Austria's ailing pension system.

- A former public prosecutor claims President Thomas Klestil, former head of staff in the Austrian foreign ministry, knew about the government's involvement in the affair surrounding the alleged murderers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989.
- Austrian trade with China declined by a third in 1996.
